derivedBy: independent model pass (c): fresh-context read of git:parity-baseline:server.js only, plus the /start body shape in public/script.js. No fixture and no other derivation was consulted.

spawn.shellNote: no { shell: true } anywhere, so the child is CreateProcess'd directly; the candidate must reproduce Node/libuv Windows argv quoting for spaces and quotes (§9 trap 3). A .cmd/.bat path cannot be spawned this way.
spawn.stdio: pipe for all three streams; the stdout/stderr handlers forward raw chunks
spawn.cwd: not specified — inherits the manager's cwd, which is where models-preset.ini is written and read
spawn.exe: body.serverPath verbatim, no existence or type check
spawn.args: body.args verbatim, in order, no filtering or reordering

orderDefect.fact: runningProcess = null runs synchronously right after arming the timer, and the timer callback re-reads the same module-level variable instead of a captured reference
orderDefect.consequenceForStop: the SIGKILL branch never runs for the process /stop was called on, because runningProcess is already null when the timer fires
orderDefect.consequenceForRelaunch: a child spawned within the 1 s window is the one the pending timer kills (Q24)
orderDefect.consequenceForRestart: /restart kills the old child, nulls runningProcess, then assigns the replacement synchronously; the old child's close handler later nulls runningProcess again, so /status settles running:false while the replacement may be alive, and the pending timer can kill it — survival is a platform race (Q23)
orderDefect.killedFlag: process.killed only reflects that a signal was delivered, not that the process exited, so /status can report running:false for a live child

state.runningProcess: module-level, single slot, no pid tracking; /status reads !!runningProcess && !runningProcess.killed
state.lastLaunchConfig: module-level { serverPath, args }; written only by /start (not by /launch-presets, not by /restart); memory only, so /restart 400s after a manager restart (Q4)
state.connectedClients: module-level array of sockets, push on connection and splice on disconnect; every emit iterates it
state.systemMetrics: module-level {cpu,ram,gpu,vram} each with usage and a 50-point history, refreshed every 1000 ms by setInterval(updateSystemMetricsHistory, 1000)
resetPoints: 'close' handler sets runningProcess = null (any child, including the replacement being nulled by the previous child)
/stop sets runningProcess = null immediately, before the child has exited

handlers.close: console.log(`Server process exited with code ${code}`); runningProcess = null; connectedClients.forEach(c => c.emit('server-ended', { message: 'Server process has ended' }))
handlers.error: console.error(`Failed to start process: ${error}`); runningProcess = null; connectedClients.forEach(c => c.emit('server-error', { message: 'Failed to start server: ' + error.message }))
handlers.stdout: const logData = data.toString(); console.log('STDOUT:', logData); emit log-stream {type:'stdout', data: logData}
handlers.stderr: const logData = data.toString(); console.log('STDERR:', logData); emit log-stream {type:'stderr', data: logData}
handlers.stdoutStderrGuards: both handlers are installed inside if (runningProcess.stdout) / if (runningProcess.stderr), which are always true with stdio: 'pipe'

exitCodes.observedSource: server.js prints the child's exit code, it never inspects or maps it
exitCodes.candidateRule: the code must be printed exactly as 'Server process exited with code <code>' including the null case for a signal-killed child
exitCodes.valuesObservedInRecordings: see SPEC/from-runtime/process-lifecycle.json — this derivation does not read fixtures

launchPresetsPath.iniFile: path.join(__dirname, 'models-preset.ini') — written on every POST /launch-presets before the serverPath guard
launchPresetsPath.portDivergence: Q5: /start's --port comes from the client (settings.serverPort), /launch-presets' from body.serverPort falling back to DEFAULT_PORT 8080
launchPresetsPath.noRunningCheck: spawn happens even if runningProcess is already set, orphaning the previous child
